speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Esophageal Perforation (Boerhaave Syndrome). The history of forceful vomiting (retching) followed by severe chest pain, combined with tachycardia and signs of pneumomediastinum, is classic for this condition. The recent doxycycline use may have contributed to pill-induced esophagitis, weakening the esophageal wall prior to the rupture. Immediate surgical consultation is required.
